messages.content: You are a clinical geneticist. You are given evidence about one rare disease and a cohort of patients described by HPO terms. Exactly one patient has the disease. Use only that evidence as your knowledge of the disease. Be explicit about which findings in the report drove each placement, and about findings that argue against it.

WEB SEARCH RESULTS FOR Alsahan-Harris syndrome (TBC1D32, OMIM:621307):

[1] Entry - #621307 - ALSAHAN-HARRIS SYNDROME; ALHAS
https://omim.org/entry/621307
Alsahan-Harris syndrome (ALHAS) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the TBC1D32 gene (615867) on chromosome 6q22.

[2] TBC1D32 gene TBC1 Domain Family Member 32
https://www.genecards.org/card/TBC1D32
Diseases associated with TBC1D32 include Orofaciodigital Syndrome Ix and Alsahan-Harris Syndrome. Among its related pathways is Ciliopathies.

https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10204718/

Task: rank the five most likely patients, most likely first, with a probability for each (they need not sum to one). For each, say which findings in the report support the placement and which argue against it, counting recorded absences as evidence; keep each to one or two sentences. Then say what the report lacked that would have made you more confident.

ranking.for: Demonstrates anophthalmia and optic nerve aplasia, directly matching the core lethal presentation noted for Alsahan-Harris syndrome, alongside abnormal sella turcica morphology consistent with TBC1D32's role in pituitary/hypothalamic development.
ranking.against: Ventriculomegaly/hydrocephaly is explicitly recorded as absent despite being noted in the disease description.

ranking.for: Presents extensive hypothalamic-pituitary defects (absent pituitary stalk, ectopic posterior pituitary, multiple hormone deficiencies) aligning with TBC1D32 expression in the hypothalamus and pituitary.
ranking.against: Lacks anophthalmia (microphthalmia recorded absent) and survived to age 12, whereas Alsahan-Harris syndrome is reported as causing neonatal death; findings align more closely with Orofaciodigital syndrome IX.

ranking.for: Exhibits hydrocephalus and ventriculomegaly, which were documented in neonates with Alsahan-Harris syndrome.
ranking.against: Anophthalmia is not observed, the patient is alive at age 10 years, and there are no recorded hypothalamic-pituitary or ciliary laterality defects.

ranking.for: Presents severe perinatal midline anomalies including encephalocele and polydactyly consistent with severe ciliopathies.
ranking.against: Lacks the hallmark anophthalmia, hydrocephaly, or documented pituitary/sella abnormalities.

ranking.for: Exhibits orofaciodigital spectrum features (bifid/lobulated tongue, accessory oral frenulum) associated with TBC1D32 ciliopathy spectrum disorders.
ranking.against: Lacks anophthalmia, hydrocephalus, or hypothalamic-pituitary abnormalities, and is alive at 9 years of age.

rounds.what_the_report_lacked: The report lacked a comprehensive clinical synopsis for OMIM:621307, the complete spectrum of visceral anomalies (e.g., laterality defects) seen in Alsahan-Harris syndrome, and explicit phenotypic differentiation between Alsahan-Harris syndrome and Orofaciodigital syndrome IX.

ranking.for: Demonstrates extensive hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction (absent pituitary stalk, ectopic posterior pituitary, combined GH, TSH, ACTH, and LHRH deficiencies) directly matching TBC1D32's role in hypothalamic-pituitary development, alongside classic orofaciodigital ciliopathy features including a lobulated tongue, accessory oral frenulum, cleft palate, and polydactyly.
ranking.against: Is 12 years old without anophthalmia or hydrocephalus, contrasting with initial reports of early lethality, hydrocephaly, and anophthalmia.

ranking.for: Exhibits prominent orofaciodigital ciliopathy manifestations such as lobulated tongue, bifid tongue, cleft palate, and accessory oral frenulum.
ranking.against: Lacks the characteristic pituitary/hypothalamic defects, anophthalmia, or hydrocephaly associated with TBC1D32 mutations.

ranking.for: Presents with anophthalmia and abnormal sella turcica morphology, partially aligning with severe perinatal ciliopathy manifestations noted in OMIM records for TBC1D32.
ranking.against: Explicitly lacks ventriculomegaly/hydrocephaly (which was highlighted in OMIM) and has uncharacteristic findings like arhinia and situs inversus totalis.

ranking.for: Features severe midline ciliopathy defects including encephalocele, preaxial foot polydactyly, and midline facial abnormalities.
ranking.against: Lacks endocrine, pituitary, or orofaciodigital features such as cleft palate, tongue abnormalities, or anophthalmia.

ranking.for: Exhibits a ciliopathy spectrum phenotype featuring postaxial polydactyly and developmental delay.
ranking.against: Has a classic Joubert syndrome presentation with a molar tooth sign and cerebellar vermis hypoplasia rather than orofaciodigital or hypothalamic-pituitary dysplasia.

rounds.what_the_report_lacked: The search results lacked a comprehensive phenotypic profile for Alsahan-Harris syndrome (OMIM:621307), specifically omitting the detailed clinical description of the expanded survivable phenotype, the frequency of hypothalamic-pituitary axis disruption versus classical orofaciodigital features, and full details of the simplex cases described in recent literature.

ranking.for: Presentation of combined pituitary hormone deficiencies (absent pituitary stalk, ectopic posterior pituitary, ACTH/TSH/GH/LHRH deficiencies) directly aligns with the report noting TBC1D32 expression in the developing hypothalamus and pituitary, alongside hallmark orofaciodigital ciliopathy features including lobulated tongue, accessory oral frenulum, submucous cleft palate, and both preaxial and postaxial polydactyly.
ranking.against: Coloboma and microphthalmia are recorded as absent despite ocular phenotypes seen in related ciliopathies.

ranking.for: Features anophthalmia, low-set ears, midface retrusion, and abnormal sella turcica morphology consistent with the severe eye and cranial ciliopathy spectrum mentioned in the report.
ranking.against: Lacks the orofaciodigital oral hallmarks, and ventriculomegaly/hydrocephalus as well as hypothalamic dysgenesis are recorded as explicitly absent.

ranking.for: Presents classic orofaciodigital ciliopathy signs related to TBC1D32 such as lobulated tongue, bifid tongue, cleft palate, and accessory oral frenulum.
ranking.against: Absence of any documented polydactyly, ocular involvement, or hypothalamic-pituitary endocrinopathies.

ranking.for: Exhibits preaxial polydactyly and an encephalocele typical of severe ciliopathies.
ranking.against: Lacks pituitary or hypothalamic involvement and has absence of corpus callosum agenesis and hand polydactyly.

ranking.for: Exhibits a bifid tongue, hypertelorism, and digital anomalies indicative of an orofaciodigital phenotype.
ranking.against: Orofacial clefting and syndactyly are explicitly recorded as absent, with no documented pituitary or hypothalamic manifestations.

rounds.what_the_report_lacked: The report lacked detailed clinical synopses of Alsahan-Harris syndrome itself, specifically the full delineation of its core endocrine and orofaciodigital findings in contrast to Orofaciodigital Syndrome IX.
